$comment: Sublease and roommate agreement. Same discipline as lease.json: jurisdiction-neutral drafting, no assertions about what any law requires, and a [bracketed blank] wherever a number is a legal judgement. In this package the wizard's tenantName answer is the OTHER person: the subtenant on a sublease, the roommate on a roommate agreement.

clauses.title: Parties and Premises
clauses.rationale: Names the layer cake plainly: the tenant on the original lease becomes the sublandlord here, and stays on the hook to the landlord above.
clauses.body: This Sublease Agreement is entered into as of {{date}} between {{company}} (“Tenant”), who rents the premises at {{propertyAddress}} (the “Premises”) under a lease with [landlord’s name] dated [date of the original lease] (the “Original Lease”), and {{tenantName}} (“Subtenant”). Tenant subleases the Premises to Subtenant on the terms below.

clauses.title: Landlord’s Consent
clauses.rationale: Most leases forbid subletting without consent, and a sublease signed without it can unravel the whole arrangement. The clause makes the sublease itself conditional on that consent existing, so the parties cannot skip the question.
clauses.body: Tenant states that the Original Lease [permits subletting / requires the landlord’s written consent, which is attached to this Sublease Agreement]. If the Original Lease requires consent and it has not been obtained, this Sublease Agreement does not take effect.

clauses.title: The Original Lease Controls
clauses.rationale: A sublease cannot give the subtenant more than the tenant has. Attaching the Original Lease and binding the subtenant to it is what makes the arrangement coherent.
clauses.body: This Sublease Agreement is subject to the Original Lease, a copy of which Subtenant has received. Subtenant will not do anything that would put Tenant in breach of the Original Lease, and Subtenant’s rights end if the Original Lease ends, whatever the reason.

clauses.title: Rent
clauses.rationale: Subtenant pays the tenant, not the landlord — keeping the money path aligned with the obligation path.
clauses.body: Subtenant will pay Tenant rent of {{monthlyRent}} per month, due in advance on the [1st] day of each month, by [payment method]. Rent for any partial month is prorated by the day. Tenant remains responsible for paying rent under the Original Lease.

clauses.title: Term
clauses.rationale: The one hard boundary of any sublease: it cannot outlast the lease it hangs from.
clauses.body: The sublease runs from [start date] to [end date]. The end date may not be later than the end of the Original Lease’s term. If the Original Lease ends earlier for any reason, this Sublease Agreement ends on the same day.

clauses.title: Security Deposit
clauses.rationale: Included only when the wizard names a deposit. Deposit rules differ from place to place; the return window is a blank to check locally.
clauses.body: Subtenant will pay Tenant a security deposit of {{securityDeposit}}, held as security for Subtenant’s performance. Within [number] days after the sublease ends and Subtenant returns possession, Tenant will return the deposit less any amounts properly withheld for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear, with an itemized written statement of anything withheld.

clauses.title: Care of the Premises
clauses.rationale: The subtenant steps into the tenant’s duties of care; repairs still flow up the chain to whoever owes them under the Original Lease.
clauses.body: Subtenant will keep the Premises clean and sanitary, use them only as a private residence, follow the rules of the Original Lease, and promptly tell Tenant in writing about any condition needing repair. Repairs are handled as the Original Lease provides; Tenant will pass repair requests to the landlord without unreasonable delay.

clauses.title: No Further Subletting
clauses.rationale: Stops the chain at one link — a sub-sublease multiplies everyone’s risk and is almost never what the original landlord agreed to.
clauses.body: Subtenant will not assign this Sublease Agreement, sublet the Premises further, or offer the Premises for short-term stays (including through rental platforms), without the prior written consent of both Tenant and the landlord.

clauses.title: Utilities
clauses.rationale: Utilities in a sublease usually stay in the tenant’s name, so the split is stated rather than assumed.
clauses.body: Utility accounts remain in [Tenant’s / Subtenant’s] name. Subtenant will pay [all utilities / the following share of utilities: [describe]] by [reimbursing Tenant within [number] days of receiving a copy of each bill / paying providers directly].

clauses.title: Entry and Move-Out
clauses.rationale: Mirrors the lease’s entry and move-out expectations one level down, with the notice period left as the same local judgement.
clauses.body: Tenant (or the landlord, as the Original Lease allows) may enter to inspect or make repairs after at least [24 hours’] notice, entering at reasonable times, and without notice in an emergency. At the end of the sublease, Subtenant will return all keys, remove all belongings, and leave the Premises in the condition received, normal wear and tear excepted.

clauses.title: Who This Agreement Is Between
clauses.rationale: A roommate agreement binds the people sharing the home to each other. It does not change anyone’s lease with the landlord, and saying so up front prevents the most common misunderstanding about what this document is.
clauses.body: This Roommate Agreement is entered into as of {{date}} between {{company}} and {{tenantName}} (together, the “Roommates”), who share the home at {{propertyAddress}}. This agreement is between the Roommates only — it does not change anyone’s lease with the landlord or make the landlord a party.

clauses.title: Rent Split
clauses.rationale: The number one roommate dispute, settled in writing: who pays how much, to whom, by when.
clauses.body: The total monthly rent for the home is {{monthlyRent}}. The Roommates split it as follows: [names and amounts — e.g. each pays half]. Each Roommate pays their share by the [day] of each month to [the roommate who pays the landlord / the landlord directly, as the lease provides].

clauses.title: Security Deposit Shares
clauses.rationale: Tracks whose money sits in the landlord’s deposit so it comes back to the right people, less each person’s own damage.
clauses.body: Of the {{securityDeposit}} security deposit held by the landlord, each Roommate contributed: [names and amounts]. When the deposit is returned, each Roommate receives their contribution back, less deductions attributable to that Roommate’s own damage or unpaid share.

clauses.title: Utilities and Shared Expenses
clauses.rationale: Names the accounts and the split, and the settle-up rhythm that keeps small imbalances from compounding into resentment.
clauses.body: The Roommates split the following recurring expenses [equally / as follows: [describe]]: [electricity, gas, water, internet, streaming — edit to match]. The account for each is held by: [names]. Whoever pays a shared bill shows it to the others, and the Roommates settle up by the [day] of each month.

clauses.title: Cleaning and Shared Spaces
clauses.rationale: Offered, not automatic — some households want the chore wheel in writing and some find it insulting. The user decides which household this is.
clauses.body: The Roommates will keep shared spaces (kitchen, bathroom, living room) reasonably clean, on the following arrangement: [describe — e.g. alternating weeks]. Personal spaces are each Roommate’s own responsibility.

clauses.title: Guests and Quiet Hours
clauses.rationale: The two flashpoints of shared living, offered with blanks rather than imposed defaults — households differ too much for a template to guess.
clauses.body: Overnight guests are fine up to [number] nights per month per Roommate; longer or more frequent stays need the other Roommates’ agreement. Quiet hours are [10pm–8am on weeknights — edit to match].

clauses.title: If a Roommate Moves Out
clauses.rationale: The scenario this document exists for. Leaving the home does not by itself end anyone’s obligations on the lease — the clause makes the departing person’s duties explicit instead of leaving them to a shrug.
clauses.body: A Roommate who wants to move out will give the others at least [30] days’ written notice. Moving out does not end that Roommate’s obligations under the lease with the landlord — those continue until the lease allows them to end. The departing Roommate remains responsible for their share of rent and expenses through the notice period, and the Roommates will cooperate in good faith on a replacement acceptable to the landlord.

clauses.title: Belongings
clauses.rationale: Offered for households that share furniture or split big purchases — who owns the couch is a real question the day someone moves out.
clauses.body: Each Roommate keeps what they brought and what they buy alone. Items bought together are owned in the shares paid, listed here as they are acquired: [item — who paid what]. When someone moves out, jointly owned items are [bought out at fair value / sold and split / decided by agreement].
